questions.def: 'Few' implies plural, requiring a plural verb 'offer'.
questions.question: Few of the submitted proposals ___ viable solutions to the problem.

questions.def: 'Amount' is used with uncountable nouns like 'research'.
questions.question: A considerable ___ of research is still needed to validate these findings.

questions.def: 'A number' indicates a plural subject requiring a plural verb.
questions.question: Only ___ of the applicants possessed the required qualifications.

questions.def: 'Little' refers to an uncountable noun, requiring a singular verb.
questions.question: Little evidence ___ to support the claim of widespread fraud.

questions.def: 'Several' is used to indicate more than two people.
questions.question: ___ of the committee members were in attendance at the crucial meeting.

questions.def: 'The majority' correctly identifies the group of respondents.
questions.question: The ___ of respondents favored the proposed changes.

questions.def: 'Deal' is used with uncountable nouns like 'time'.
questions.question: A good ___ of time was spent analyzing the data.

questions.def: 'A handful of' suggests a very small number.
questions.question: Only ___ students managed to pass the rigorous exam.

questions.def: 'Amount' is used with uncountable nouns like 'funding'.
questions.question: A significant ___ of funding is required for this project.

questions.def: 'Quite a few' means a considerable number.
questions.question: Quite ___ people attended the lecture, despite the bad weather.

questions.def: 'Some' is used with uncountable nouns like 'information'.
questions.question: ___ of the information provided was actually useful for the project.

questions.def: 'A limited number' refers to countable items like seats.
questions.question: Only ___ of seats are available for the concert.

questions.def: 'Scarcely any' implies almost none.
questions.question: Scarcely ___ of the participants understood the complex instructions.

questions.def: 'Limited' indicates a small amount of agreement.
questions.question: There is ___ consensus among experts on this particular issue.

questions.def: 'A minority' indicates a smaller portion of a group.
questions.question: Only ___ of the population voted in the election.

questions.def: 'Hardly any' implies almost none.
questions.question: Hardly ___ of the books in the library were undamaged.

questions.def: 'Insufficient' means not enough research.
questions.question: ___ research has been conducted in this specific area.

questions.def: 'A small portion' correctly refers to a part of the budget.
questions.question: Only ___ of the budget was allocated to marketing.

questions.def: 'Proportion' indicates a fraction or percentage.
questions.question: A significant ___ of the budget is allocated to research.

questions.def: Percentage goes with a quantifiable amount.
questions.question: Only ___ of the applicants possessed all the necessary skills.

questions.def: Should be 'Few students' because the word is countable
questions.question: Little students attended the optional lecture today.

questions.def: 'Volume' implies a large quantity of uncountable items.
questions.question: A large ___ of data was collected during the experiment.

questions.def: 'Number' is used with countable nouns like 'seats'.
questions.question: A limited ___ of seats are available for the seminar.

questions.def: 'Modicum' implies a very small quantity.
questions.question: ___ of the evidence supports the defendant's claims.

questions.def: 'Few' implies a plural subject, requiring the plural verb 'possess'.
questions.question: Few of the applicants ___ the necessary qualifications for the role.

questions.def: 'Little' refers to a small amount of something uncountable like 'research'.
questions.question: ___ research has been conducted to explore this phenomenon fully.

questions.def: 'Handful' is the correct noun to represent a small quantity of people.
questions.question: Only a ___ of scientists understood the implications of the study.

questions.def: 'Scant' implies a very small, barely sufficient amount of evidence.
questions.question: There is ___ evidence to support the claim, despite initial optimism.

questions.def: 'Hardly any' means almost none, appropriately modifying 'data'.
questions.question: ___ of the data collected was actually useful for the analysis.

questions.def: 'Modicum' means a small amount and fits the context of a budget allocation.
questions.question: Only a ___ of the budget was allocated to marketing.
